                            I: INTRODUCTION

1. This judgment is pronounced in Criminal Case No. 538550/2016, arising out of FIR No. 410/2004 registered at Police Station Model Town (Crime Branch), Delhi, under Sections 420/468/471/120-B/411 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("IPC"). The case was investigated by the Special Team, Crime Branch, Prashant Vihar, Delhi, under the supervision of ASI Ram Kumar (PW-19).

2. The present case has had a chequered and protracted history spanning over two decades, commencing from the registration of the FIR on 13.07.2004 and culminating in the recording of the statement of the accused under ANURADHA JINDAL Digitally signed by ANURADHA FIR No. 410/04 State Vs. Dalip Kumar Page 2 of 48 JINDAL Date: 2026.05.30 16:45:01 +0530 Section 313 Cr.P.C. on 21.01.2025, followed by the hearing of final arguments. The case involves a well-organised credit card fraud perpetrated through criminal conspiracy, impersonation, forgery, and cheating, targeting bonafide customers of Standard Chartered Bank. The accused persons before this Court, and their respective status, are as follows:

2026.05.30 16:45:05 +0530 FIR No. 410/04 State Vs. Dalip Kumar Page 3 of 48 II: BRIEF FACTS A. Prosecution's Case

4. The prosecution's case, as disclosed in the complaint (Ex. PW-4/A) filed by Sh. Tushar Dhar (PW-4), Regional Officer, Fraud Control Unit, Standard Chartered Bank, and as established through the evidence of nineteen prosecution witnesses examined during the course of the trial, is summarised as follows:

Background and Genesis of the Case

5. In the year 2004, a well-organised and premeditated criminal conspiracy was hatched by the accused persons, who exploited their insider knowledge of the banking system to defraud bonafide credit card holders of Standard Chartered Bank. The conspiracy was made possible by the fact that accused S.M. Vipul was employed as a Customer Satisfaction Executive at the BankCard Customer Satisfaction Centre of Standard Chartered Bank, 3rd Floor, Express Building, 9-10, Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg, New Delhi. By virtue of his employment, accused S.M. Vipul had access to confidential customer data, including credit card numbers, expiry dates, personal details of cardholders, and blank letterheads of the bank. He misused this access to facilitate the criminal conspiracy.

The Modus Operandi

6. The scheme devised by the accused persons was sophisticated and multi- layered, involving the following steps:

 Obtaining confidential details of Standard Chartered Bank credit card holders through accused S.M. Vipul, who was an employee of the said Digitally signed by bank; ANURADHA ANURADHA JINDAL JINDAL Date:
2026.05.30 16:45:10 +0530 FIR No. 410/04 State Vs. Dalip Kumar Page 4 of 48  Impersonating bank officials and telephonically contacting credit card holders, informing them of alleged fraudulent or unauthorised transactions on their cards, thereby creating a sense of urgency and alarm in the minds of the victims;
 Visiting the card holders' offices or residences with forged letters printed on blank Standard Chartered Bank letterheads, purportedly signed by fictitious bank officials, to lend an air of authenticity to the deception;
 Collecting the original credit cards from the card holders on the false pretext of issuing fresh or replacement cards, thereby obtaining physical possession of the cards;
 Thereafter, using the fraudulently obtained credit cards at various shops in Delhi to purchase high-value electronic goods, mobile phones, motorcycles, and other articles, causing substantial wrongful loss to the victims and wrongful gain to the accused persons.
Victim/ Sh. Ramesh Ranade (PW-1)

7. On 18.06.2004, PW-1 received a telephonic call from a person who introduced himself as an official of the Fraud Control Unit of Standard Chartered Bank. The caller informed PW-1 that an internet transaction of Rs. 11,230/- had been made from his credit card (No. 4129-0576-8059- 5798) without his authorisation, and that the bank was taking steps to protect his account. This call was designed to create anxiety in the mind of PW-1 and to prepare the ground for the subsequent visit.

8. On 21.06.2004, accused Jaspreet Singh visited PW-1's office at 85, Model Basti, New Delhi. He introduced himself as "Raman Preet Singh," an employee of the Fraud Control Unit of Standard Chartered Bank, and produced a forged letter dated 19.06.2004 on a Standard Chartered Bank ANURADHA JINDAL Digitally signed FIR No. 410/04 State Vs. Dalip Kumar Page 5 of 48 by ANURADHA JINDAL Date: 2026.05.30 16:45:16 +0530 letterhead (Mark X1), along with a fake identity card, to establish his false credentials. He informed PW-1 that his credit card had been compromised and that it was necessary to collect the card and issue a fresh one. Trusting the representations made by the accused, PW-1 handed over his credit card to the accused. As a precaution, PW-1 obtained a photocopy of his credit card and took the signature of the accused on the photocopy as a receipt. The accused signed the photocopy in the name of "Raman Preet Singh."

9. Subsequently, PW-1 received a credit card statement revealing purchases of over Rs. 2,00,000/- made using his card at various establishments, including Dee Aar Electronics (Sony Ericsson P-900, Rs. 38,600/-), Jaina Sales Corporation (two Sony Ericsson P900 handsets, Rs. 38,500/- each), Amit Communications (Nokia 1100, Rs. 4,050/-), and Standard Chartered Airport Service Station (Rs. 200/-), among others. PW-1 had not authorised any of these transactions.

Victim/ Sh. L.N. Jhunjhunwala (PW-3)

10.On 28.05.2004, Sh. L.N. Jhunjhunwala, Chairman of LNJ Bhilwara Group, sent a letter to Standard Chartered Bank to surrender his credit card (No. 5543-7586-8065-4239). On 31.05.2004, a person identifying himself as "Vinod" visited the office at Noida, produced a forged letter (Ex. PW-3/A) purportedly signed by "Rajeev Roy, Manager Customer Accounts," and collected the original credit card from PW-5 (Suresh Nair, Junior Executive). Subsequently, transactions of approximately Rs. 2,00,000/- were found to have been made on the said card, including the purchase of Nokia mobile phones at Orange Tele Services and footwear at Style Shoes.

11.A similar modus operandi was employed to fraudulently obtain the credit card of Sh. Mohd. Nural Islam (Card No. 4129-0586-8369-3549). Two forged letters were handed over to him by accused Dalip Kumar, impersonating a bank agent. Fraudulent internet transactions of Rs. 6,103/- and Rs. 5,980.08/- were subsequently made on his card through Stormpay Inc. Arrest of Accused Dalip Kumar and His Disclosure

12.On 13.07.2004, acting on the complaint of Sh. Tushar Dhar (PW-4), a raiding party comprising IO/ASI Ram Kumar (PW-19), HC Satyawan (PW-11), Ct. Jai Singh (PW-18), and the complainant proceeded to Model Town-II, in front of Naveen Electronics. Accused Dalip Kumar was apprehended while riding a motorcycle (No. DL-3SAE-9172), which he had himself purchased using the fraudulently obtained credit card of Sh. L.N. Jhunjhunwala. Two Standard Chartered Bank credit cards belonging to Mohd. Nural Islam and Subimal Guha Roy were recovered from his possession and seized vide Ex. PW-4/B. Accused Dalip Kumar disclosed that he had purchased the motorcycle and mobile phones using the credit card of Sh. L.N. Jhunjhunwala, and further disclosed the role of accused Jaspreet Singh in the conspiracy.

Arrest of Accused Jaspreet Singh

13.At the instance and on the disclosure of accused Dalip Kumar, accused Jaspreet Singh was arrested from A-Block, near Ram Park, Lajpat Nagar, vide arrest memo Ex. PW-4/G. Significantly, no recovery was effected from accused Jaspreet Singh at the time of his arrest or thereafter. The Digitally signed by ANURADHA ANURADHA JINDAL JINDAL Date:

2026.05.30 16:45:28 FIR No. 410/04 State Vs. Dalip Kumar Page 7 of 48 +0530 prosecution's case against him rests primarily on the direct testimony of PW-1 and the scientific evidence of the FSL Report.
Arrest of Accused S.M. Vipul and Recovery of Blank Letterheads

14.At the instance of accused Dalip Kumar, accused S.M. Vipul was subsequently arrested. From the briefcase recovered from his room at A-74, Lajpat Nagar Part-I, two blank letterheads of Standard Chartered Bank were seized vide Ex. PW-4/F (Ex. P-3 and Ex. P-4). This recovery is of critical significance as it establishes the link between accused S.M. Vipul and the forged documents used in the commission of the offences. Accused S.M. Vipul was an employee of Standard Chartered Bank and had provided blank letterheads and credit card holder details to his co- conspirators, thereby facilitating the entire criminal enterprise.

Recovery of Stolen Goods

15.At the instance of accused Dalip Kumar, from his house, three Nokia mobile phones, one LG colour TV, one Philips music system, and two speakers were recovered and seized vide Ex. PW-11/A. One computer system (HP) was also recovered from the house of S.M. Vipul at the instance of accused Dalip Kumar, seized vide Ex. PW-11/C. These recoveries corroborate the prosecution's case that the fraudulently obtained credit cards were used to purchase high-value goods.

FSL Report

16.Documents including questioned documents (Q1 to Q21), specimen signatures of accused Dilip Kumar (S1-S42) and Jaspreet Singh (S43- S48), and admitted signatures of the victims were sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL), Delhi. The FSL Report (Ex. PW-15/A) was Digitally signed by ANURADHA ANURADHA JINDAL JINDAL Date:

2026.05.30 FIR No. 410/04 State Vs. Dalip Kumar Page 8 of 48 16:45:35 +0530 submitted by PW-15, Sh. Devak Ram, Senior Scientific Assistant, Document Division, FSL, Delhi. The FSL Report, insofar as it is relevant to accused Jaspreet Singh, opined that the person who wrote specimen signatures S43 to S48 (of Jaspreet Singh) also wrote questioned signatures Q19 and Q20, with significant similarities observed in writing habits, movement, skill, speed, spacing, alignment, and character formation. The questioned signatures Q19 and Q20 are the signatures of "Raman Preet Singh" on the forged letter (Mark X1) and on the photocopy of the credit card (Mark X3) respectively.
B. Defence's Version

17.Accused Jaspreet Singh, in his statement recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. on 21.01.2025, denied all the incriminating circumstances put to him. His specific responses were as follows:

 He denied visiting the office of Sh. Ramesh Ranade on 21.06.2004 or impersonating "Raman Preet Singh."  He denied entering into any criminal conspiracy with accused Dalip Kumar or S.M. Vipul.
 He denied procuring blank letterheads from accused S.M. Vipul or forging any letter.
 He stated that the witnesses were "mostly police officials and interested witnesses."
 He claimed to be innocent and stated that he had been falsely framed.  He declined to lead any defence evidence.

18.It is pertinent to note that the defence of the accused is a bare denial, devoid of any specific explanation of the incriminating circumstances appearing against him in the prosecution evidence. The accused has not offered any Digitally signed by ANURADHA ANURADHA JINDAL JINDAL Date:

2026.05.30 FIR No. 410/04 State Vs. Dalip Kumar Page 9 of 48 16:45:40 +0530 explanation as to why PW-1 would falsely identify him as the person who visited his office and collected his credit card. He has not offered any explanation as to why his specimen signatures match the questioned signatures on the forged documents, as per the FSL Report. He has not suggested any alternative hypothesis that could explain the incriminating circumstances on record.
III: PROCEDURAL HISTORY

19.The case has had a protracted procedural history spanning over two decades. The delay in the conclusion of the trial is attributable to a combination of factors, including the large number of witnesses examined by the prosecution, the death of one accused, the abscondence of another, the recalling of witnesses under Section 311 Cr.P.C., and the change of the presiding officer at the stage of final arguments.                            IV: CHARGES FRAMED

20.The following charges were framed against accused Jaspreet Singh on 09.09.2013:

20.1. First Charge/ Section 419/420 IPC: That on 21.06.2004, accused Jaspreet Singh impersonated "Raman Preet Singh," an employee of Standard Chartered Bank, and induced Sh. Ramesh Ranade to hand over his credit card on the pretext of issuing a fresh card, thereby committing cheating by personation and dishonestly inducing delivery of property.
20.2. Second Charge/ Section 419/420 read with Section 120-B IPC: That on or prior to 13.07.2004, accused Jaspreet Singh entered into a criminal conspiracy with accused Dalip Kumar (P.O.) and used the credit cards of Sh. L.N. Jhunjhunwala, Sh. Ramesh Ranade, and Sh. Mohd. Nural Islam at various shops for purchasing television sets, mobile phones, music systems, and other articles, thereby causing wrongful loss to the card holders and wrongful gain to the accused persons.
20.3. Third Charge/ Sections 468/471 IPC: That on or prior to 21.06.2004, accused Jaspreet Singh procured a blank Standard Chartered Bank Digitally signed by ANURADHA ANURADHA JINDAL JINDAL Date:
2026.05.30 FIR No. 410/04 State Vs. Dalip Kumar Page 11 of 48 16:45:51 +0530 letterhead from accused S.M. Vipul, forged the letter dated 19.06.2004, signed the same in the name of "Raman Preet Singh," and dishonestly and fraudulently used the said forged letter as genuine at the time of obtaining the credit card from Sh. Ramesh Ranade.
21.Both accused Jaspreet Singh and S.M. Vipul pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

V: ISSUES FOR DETERMINATION

22.The following issues arise for determination in the present case:

22.1. Whether the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that accused Jaspreet Singh, on 21.06.2004, impersonated "Raman Preet Singh" and dishonestly induced Sh. Ramesh Ranade to deliver his credit card, thereby committing offences punishable under Sections 419 and 420 IPC?
22.2. Whether the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that accused Jaspreet Singh entered into a criminal conspiracy with accused Dalip Kumar (P.O.) on or prior to 13.07.2004, and in furtherance thereof, used the credit cards of Sh. L.N. Jhunjhunwala, Sh. Ramesh Ranade, and Sh. Mohd. Nural Islam at various shops, thereby committing offences punishable under Sections 419/420 read with Section 120-B IPC?
22.3. Whether the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that accused Jaspreet Singh forged the letter dated 19.06.2004 on a Standard Chartered Bank letterhead, signed the same in the name of "Raman Preet Singh," and used the said forged document as genuine, thereby committing offences punishable under Sections 468 and 471 IPC? ANURADHA JINDAL 22.4. What is the effect of the non-recovery of any incriminating article from Digitally signed accused Jaspreet Singh at the time of his arrest or thereafter? by ANURADHA JINDAL Date: 2026.05.30 16:45:58 +0530 FIR No. 410/04 State Vs. Dalip Kumar Page 12 of 48 22.5. Whether the prosecution has proved its case against accused Jaspreet Singh beyond reasonable doubt?

VI: EVIDENCE ANALYSIS A. Oral Evidence PW-1: Sh. Ramesh Ranade (Complainant/Primary Victim)

23.PW-1 is the primary victim in respect of accused Jaspreet Singh and his testimony is the cornerstone of the prosecution's case against this accused. He deposed that on 18.06.2004, he received a telephonic call from a person claiming to be from the Fraud Control Unit of Standard Chartered Bank, informing him of an unauthorised transaction of Rs. 11,230/-. On 21.06.2004, a person came to his office at 85, Model Basti, New Delhi, introduced himself as "Raman Preet Singh," produced a letter dated 19.06.2004 on a Standard Chartered Bank letterhead along with an identity card, and collected his credit card. He obtained a photocopy of his credit card and took the signature of the said person on the photocopy as a receipt. He subsequently received a credit card statement showing purchases of over Rs. 2,00,000/-. He identified accused Jaspreet Singh in Court as the person who had visited his office and collected his credit card. He identified the documents Mark X1 (letter dated 19.06.2004), Mark X2 (envelope), Mark X3 (photocopy of credit card with signatures of "Raman Preet Singh"), and other documents seized vide Ex. PW-1/A.

24.PW-1 was recalled and re-examined on 20.05.2023 pursuant to the order dated 07.03.2023 passed on the application under Section 311 Cr.P.C. filed by accused Jaspreet Singh, and was subjected to further cross-examination. The fact that the accused himself sought the recalling of PW-1 for further Digitally signed by ANURADHA ANURADHA JINDAL JINDAL Date:

2026.05.30 FIR No. 410/04 State Vs. Dalip Kumar Page 13 of 48 16:46:07 +0530 cross-examination, and availed of the opportunity to test his testimony, lends additional credibility to the prosecution's case, as the accused was given every opportunity to challenge the testimony of the primary witness against him.

25.In cross-examination, PW-1 admitted that there were no CCTV cameras at his office. He admitted that the credit card statement did not reflect the name of Jaspreet Singh or Raman Preet Singh, only the amount. He denied that the accused never visited his office and denied deposing falsely.

26.Court's Assessment: The testimony of PW-1 is direct, consistent, and cogent. He is the victim himself and has no discernible motive to falsely implicate the accused. His in-court identification of accused Jaspreet Singh as the person who visited his office on 21.06.2004 and collected his credit card is a piece of direct evidence of the highest order. The identification is not a dock identification made for the first time in Court; it is supported by the fact that PW-1 had a face-to-face interaction with the accused at his office, during which the accused produced documents and engaged in a conversation with PW-1, giving PW-1 ample opportunity to observe and remember the accused's features.

27.The absence of CCTV footage is a neutral circumstance and does not, by itself, dislodge the direct testimony of the victim. The fact that the credit card statement does not reflect the name of the accused is also a neutral circumstance, as credit card statements typically reflect only the transaction amounts and merchant names, not the identity of the person who used the card. The corroboration provided by the FSL Report, which ANURADHA scientifically links the specimen signatures of accused Jaspreet Singh to theJINDAL questioned signatures on the forged letter (Mark X1) and the photocopy of Digitally signed by ANURADHA JINDAL Date: 2026.05.30 FIR No. 410/04 State Vs. Dalip Kumar Page 14 of 48 16:46:14 +0530 the credit card (Mark X3), is a powerful piece of corroborative evidence that reinforces the credibility of PW-1's testimony.

28.Minor inconsistencies in dates do not materially affect the substance of his testimony. Such minor discrepancies are natural in the testimony of a witness who is deposing about events that occurred several years prior to the date of his examination, and do not, by themselves, render the testimony unreliable.

PW-2: SI Virender Kumar

29.PW-2 proved the registration of FIR No. 410/2004 (Ex. PW-2/A) and the endorsement on the rukka (Ex. PW-2/B). His testimony is formal in nature and establishes the factum of registration of the FIR. He was not cross- examined on any material point. His testimony is accepted as proved.

PW-3: Sh. L.N. Jhunjhunwala

30.PW-3 deposed that he had sent a letter to Standard Chartered Bank on 28.05.2004 to surrender his credit card and confirmed that his junior executive handed over the credit card to a bank representative who produced a letter (Ex. PW-3/A). He admitted in cross-examination that he was not personally present at the time of handing over the card and that the bank absorbed the financial liability. His testimony is limited in scope and is more relevant to the conspiracy charge than to the specific charge against accused Jaspreet Singh. However, his testimony establishes the existence of the credit card and the fact that it was surrendered to an impersonator, which is consistent with the prosecution's case regarding the modus operandi of the conspiracy. 31.PW-4 was the Regional Officer, Fraud Control Unit, Standard Chartered Bank, and the original complainant. He deposed about filing the complaint (Ex. PW-4/A), participating in the raid at Naveen Electronics where accused Dalip Kumar was apprehended, the recovery of two credit cards (Ex. P-1 and Ex. P-2) from accused Dalip Kumar, and the subsequent recovery of two blank Standard Chartered Bank letterheads (Ex. P-3 and Ex. P-4) from the briefcase of accused S.M. Vipul. He correctly identified accused Jaspreet Singh in Court and confirmed that S.M. Vipul was an employee of Standard Chartered Bank.
32.PW-4 was further cross-examined on 11.04.2023 pursuant to the order on the Section 311 Cr.P.C. application. In cross-examination, he admitted that accused Jaspreet Singh was not present at the time of the raid at Naveen Electronics and that Jaspreet Singh was arrested solely at the instance of accused Dilip Kumar, without any independent corroboration at the time of arrest.
33.Court's Assessment: PW-4 is a material witness who provides the institutional perspective on the fraud and corroborates the chain of events leading to the arrest of the accused persons. His testimony regarding the recovery of blank letterheads from S.M. Vipul's premises is of critical significance in establishing the conspiracy. The admission that Jaspreet Singh was arrested solely at the instance of Dilip Kumar is a factor that has been carefully considered by this Court. However, this admission must be read in the context of the entire evidence on record. The arrest of an accused at the instance of a co-accused does not, by itself, create a ANURADHA JINDAL reasonable doubt as to the guilt of the arrested accused, particularly when Digitally signed by ANURADHA JINDAL Date: FIR No. 410/04 State Vs. Dalip Kumar Page 16 of 48 2026.05.30 16:46:28 +0530 the prosecution's case is independently corroborated by the direct testimony of the victim (PW-1) and the scientific evidence of the FSL Report.

PW-5: Sh. Suresh Nair

34.PW-5 deposed that on 31.05.2004, a person identifying himself as "Vinod" came to the office at Noida, produced a letter (Ex. PW-3/A), and collected the original credit card of Sh. L.N. Jhunjhunwala. He was not cross- examined on any material point. His testimony establishes the fraudulent collection of Sh. Jhunjhunwala's credit card but does not directly identify accused Jaspreet Singh as the perpetrator in this instance. His testimony is relevant to the conspiracy charge and is accepted as proved.

PW-6: Sh. Jai Kumar

35.PW-6 deposed that on 28.09.2004, he visited the Crime Branch office and handed over two original letters written in the name of "Arun" and bearing the signatures of Sh. L.N. Jhunjhunwala (Ex. PW-6/B and Ex. PW-6/C), which were seized vide Ex. PW-6/A. He identified the signatures of Sh. L.N. Jhunjhunwala on both letters. He was not cross-examined on any material point.

36.Court's Assessment: The testimony of PW-6 is relevant to the prosecution's case as it forms part of the documentary trail surrounding the fraudulent collection of Sh. Jhunjhunwala's credit card. The two letters bearing the signatures of Sh. L.N. Jhunjhunwala (Ex. PW-6/B and Ex. PW-6/C) are relevant to the conspiracy charge, as they form part of the chain of correspondence and documentation surrounding the fraud. The fact that PW-6 was not cross-examined on any material point means that ANURADHA JINDAL Digitally signed by ANURADHA JINDAL FIR No. 410/04 State Vs. Dalip Kumar Page 17 of 48 Date:

2026.05.30 16:46:38 +0530
his testimony stands unrebutted and uncontroverted. His testimony, read in conjunction with the testimony of PW-3 and PW-5, corroborates the prosecution's case regarding the fraudulent collection of Sh. Jhunjhunwala's credit card and the existence of the criminal conspiracy. This Court accepts the testimony of PW-6 as proved.
PW-7: Sh. Rajesh Sharma (Area Head/ Human Resources, Standard Chartered Bank)

37.PW-7 was working as Area Head (Human Resources), North, at Standard Chartered Bank in 2005. He deposed that he submitted employment details of three employees of Standard Chartered Bank as sought by the police, and the said details were placed on record vide Ex. PW-7/A. The employment details confirmed that accused S.M. Vipul was employed as a Customer Satisfaction Executive at Standard Chartered Bank from 08.09.2003 to 03.07.2004, that accused Sharmila Bhattacharya was employed as a Customer Satisfaction Officer from 01.09.2003 to 13.07.2004, and that accused Dilip Kumar was employed as a Customer Satisfaction Associate from 01.09.2003 to 29.09.2003. PW-7 stated that he could not produce the original employment documents as he was no longer employed with the bank at the time of his deposition. His further examination-in-chief was deferred for want of original documents.

VII: LEGAL REASONING A. Applicable Statutory Provisions
80.Section 419 IPC/Punishment for Cheating by Personation: Whoever cheats by personation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. The offence of cheating by personation is complete when a person pretends to be some other person, or knowingly substitutes one person for another, or represents that he or any other person is a person other than he or such other person really is.
81.Section 420 IPC/ Cheating and Dishonestly Inducing Delivery of Property: The essential ingredients are: (i) deception of a person; (ii) fraudulent or dishonest inducement to deliver property or to alter or destroy a valuable security; and (iii) mens rea. The offence under Section 420 IPC is an aggravated form of cheating under Section 415 IPC, and is attracted when the cheating results in the delivery of property or the alteration or destruction of a valuable security.
82.Section 468 IPC/ Forgery for Purpose of Cheating: The essential ingredients are: (i) making a false document; and (ii) intent that the ANURADHA JINDAL Digitally signed by ANURADHA FIR No. 410/04 State Vs. Dalip Kumar Page 33 of 48 JINDAL Date: 2026.05.30 16:47:59 +0530 document shall be used for the purpose of cheating. 83.Section 471 IPC/ Using as Genuine a Forged Document: The essential ingredients are: (i) using a document known to be forged; (ii) using it as genuine; and (iii) fraudulent or dishonest intent.
